rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Noah account also appears at 10:71–73, while this sūra gives a much fuller treatment.
rows.anchor: The anecdote of Noah (sws) has also been referred to in verses 71-73 of the previous sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An open warner gives a grounded warning, resting on revelation and God’s established practice rather than speculation.
rows.anchor: refers to the fact that the punishment which a messenger warns his nation is not based on speculation and conjecture

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment is grounded in revelation.
rows.anchor: This is because in the first instance it is based on divine revelation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice necessarily brings punishment when His messenger is denied.
rows.anchor: which necessarily manifests itself if His messenger is denied.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s opening call mirrors the Prophet’s preaching in 11:3, and the parallel disputes bring the Prophet and companions’ present and future into view.
rows.anchor: Earlier in verse 3, precisely in the same manner the Prophet (sws) began his preaching.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correspondence between the accounts makes history instructive for the present and future; otherwise, it is only a record of past events.
rows.anchor: This is the real significance of history.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs are the nation’s leaders, who are especially hostile to prophetic reform because they have led their people astray.
rows.anchor: refers to the leaders and chiefs of a nation. Since they are the ones who have led their nation astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s opponents object that he is a mortal like them, arguing that a messenger should be an angel or have an angelic witness.
rows.anchor: Firstly, he is but a mortal like them. If God wanted to send a messenger, he should have sent an angel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh made the same demand of the Prophet in 10:12, linking their challenge with Noah’s opponents’ objection.
rows.anchor: Earlier in verse 12, it is cited that the Quraysh had made precisely the same demand from the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs disparage Noah’s followers as socially insignificant and unable to reason through consequences.
rows.anchor: Secondly, his followers are the lowly ones of the society who have no significance and respect;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents infer that Noah’s followers accepted him without using their intellect; al-Zamakhsharī reads the phrase as acting on a first impression without reflection.
rows.anchor: If they have believed in him, it is without using their intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi cites al-Zamakhsharī’s grammatical reading of the expression as an adverbial locus: the followers acted on their initial understanding without reflecting further.
rows.anchor: This means that they did what they understood in the first instance and did not care to reflect on it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs’ third objection is that a favored messenger should have worldly treasure and an entourage; their greater resources supposedly expose Noah as bluffing.
rows.anchor: He should have opened the treasure of this world to him and his companions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s clear argument is an innate divine spark, while God’s mercy is revelation; together they ground his message.
rows.anchor: one is the divine spark present innately in his nature (clear argument) and the other is divine revelation (God’s mercy)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If his opponents retained that inner spark, they would recognize Noah’s message as the voice of their own hearts; their ingratitude has darkened their hearts and blocked guidance.
rows.anchor: if his adversaries too had this divine spark in them, they would have regarded his (ie. Noah’s) message to be a call of their own hearts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah cannot force guidance on people who have no desire for it and are averse to his message.
rows.anchor: How can Noah (sws) forcibly stick something on them for which they have no thirst

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents judge value by worldly resources and wonder how Noah’s poor followers can receive a good message when they have no such means.
rows.anchor: in their eyes, the real significance of anything is based on the means and resources of life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah will not dismiss believers to protect the chiefs’ pride, since God determines a person’s real standing.
rows.anchor: he is not going to shove them away to accommodate their ego. If he does this, how would he face God in the hereafter?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 30 further explains Noah’s refusal to abandon the believers: he asks who would protect him from God if he did so.
rows.anchor: This is a further explanation of the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s reply consolidates an answer to all the opponents’ objections: he claims only to be God’s messenger, not to possess the treasures or unseen knowledge they imagine.
rows.anchor: This verse gives a consolidated answer to all the objections raised by Noah’s opponents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth is given to the worthy and unworthy alike, while religious treasure belongs to receptive hearts; material means do not prove spiritual superiority.
rows.anchor: The riches of this world are given to every person whether he is worthy of them or not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows what is within people; if Noah endorsed the chiefs’ assumption that poor believers could receive no good, he would be unjust.
rows.anchor: Only God knows what is inside a person’s heart and nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents demand the threatened punishment only after being routed in debate and receiving the truth conclusively.
rows.anchor: once they had been totally routed in discussion and debate and once the truth had been conclusively delivered to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the final preaching stage, a messenger declares his acquittal after completing his duty and leaves deniers to the fate God determines.
rows.anchor: a messenger announces his acquittal once he has discharged his duty and consigns those who have denied him to the fate

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters take the verse to address the Prophet Muḥammad within Noah’s account.
rows.anchor: Some people think that this verse addresses the Prophet (sws) and it has come within the anecdote of Noah (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi allows that reading but prefers to understand the verse as Noah’s declaration of acquittal at the end of his preaching; the nation’s fate is then sealed.
rows.anchor: in my view this verse is a declaration of acquittal at the end of the preaching phase

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation that no further people would believe and the order to build the Ark came after Noah’s declaration of acquittal.
rows.anchor: Noah (sws) was sent this revelation after the above cited declaration of acquittal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment may first jolt indifferent people into heed, or decisively destroy those who reject a messenger after the truth is conclusively delivered.
rows.anchor: the torment is of two types. One is meant to shake and jolt the indifferent and disbelieving elements of a nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Decisive punishment remains at its site, leaves a lesson in ruins and history, and foreshadows the rejecters’ punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: It is not like a wave that comes and passes. It stations itself on the place it descends.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s promise that they would be mocked in return does not mean indecent retaliation; the deniers will later weep, while Noah and his companions rejoice at God’s help.
rows.anchor: do not mean that they will also indulge in indecent mockery the way their opponents are doing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At times the wording is chosen for a matching ring although its meaning differs; in this case, jubilation at decisive punishment marks truth’s triumph and evil’s humiliation.
rows.anchor: At times, a sentence is just constructed to impart it a congruent ring to it but its meaning is different.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The storm caused abundant rain and water from nearby seas to cross onto land.
rows.anchor: It resulted in abundant rain and water from nearby seas crossed on to land.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A faithless majority is, in God’s eyes, a mass of filth that He may cleanse from the earth rather than preserve for its numbers.
rows.anchor: a majority devoid of faith is a pile filth in His eyes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers back to God’s verdict in response to Satan’s initial ultimatum, issued at the beginning.
rows.anchor: which He proclaimed before Satan on the very first day in response to his ultimatum.

rows.speaker: Farāhī
rows.claim: Farāhī’s account says the Ark was stranded on Mount Judī during the storm.
rows.anchor: In this storm, Noah’s Ark got stuck at the mount of Judī.

rows.speaker: Farāhī
rows.claim: Farāhī describes a cyclonic whirlpool wind that caused torrential rain and made the seas burst forth.
rows.anchor: Ustādh Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī writes: It is evident from these details that a cyclonic whirlpool wind visited the people of Noah (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word amr in both verses means punishment as a directive of God.
rows.anchor: means “punishment” which is a directive of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairs to be brought aboard are not every animal, including pests, but those domesticated and useful to people, as understood in context.
rows.anchor: They are spoken with respect to what is in the mind of the speaker.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those already subject to God’s verdict against Satan’s followers among humankind and jinn could not board; the others were to be taken aboard.
rows.anchor: those on whom this directive stands implemented will not be able to board this ship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small number of believers reassures the oppressed Muslim minority as a warning to Quraysh’s arrogant majority.
rows.anchor: Also found in this last part of the verse is a warning for the arrogant majority of the Quraysh and great assurance for the oppressed Muslim minority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should trust God and His mercy, not the Ark or other material means, however important those means are.
rows.anchor: believers in reality should trust God and His mercy and not these resources.
